# WCAG Check

> A free tool that checks whether a web page meets the accessibility requirements of the European Accessibility Act. It reports each problem against both its WCAG 2.2 success criterion and the corresponding EN 301 549 clause 9 reference, which is the standard the Act actually cites.

Enter a page URL and the tool fetches its HTML and runs 20 checks that can be
determined without a browser. Results are generated per request; nothing about a
scanned site is stored, and no account is needed.

## What it detects

- Images: missing alt text, alt text that is only a filename, image buttons and image map areas without alt
- Structure: no h1, skipped heading levels, no main landmark
- Forms: fields with no associated label
- Links and buttons: no accessible name, non-descriptive link text
- Document: missing title, missing lang attribute, duplicate id values, positive tabindex
- Media: video or audio without captions, media that autoplays
- Zoom: a viewport meta tag that prevents zooming
- Tables: data tables without header cells
- Frames: iframe without a title

## What it cannot detect

Because the analysis is static and executes no JavaScript, these are out of scope
and are stated as such on the page:

- Colour contrast, which requires rendered styles
- Keyboard traps and focus order, which require a real browser
- Content injected by JavaScript
- The quality of video audio descriptions

Roughly a third of accessibility requirements need human judgement. A clean
result means the machine-detectable problems are gone, not that a site is
compliant.

## Pages

- [Home and scanner](https://wcagcheck.eu/): run a check and read the report

## References

- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/): the W3C accessibility guidelines
- [EN 301 549](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/): the European standard whose clause 9 restates WCAG Level A and AA for websites
